name: Cash Flow Forecasting
title: Cash Flow Forecasting
answer: Cash flow forecasting is the practice of estimating when money will actually arrive and when it must go out, usually over the next thirteen weeks and again over the coming year. It sits inside treasury and liquidity work, where the question is not profit but whether the bank balance stays above zero on every single day. The forecast covers receivables from customers, payments to suppliers and staff, tax and interest, debt service, and the draws and repayments on any revolving facility. It is distinct from the statutory accounts, which look backwards, and from the budget, which is a plan rather than a prediction.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: Cash flow forecasting is the practice of estimating when money will actually arrive and when it must go out, usually over the next thirteen weeks and again over the coming year. It sits inside treasury and liquidity work, where the question is not profit but whether the bank balance stays above zero on every single day. The forecast covers receivables from customers, payments to suppliers and staff, tax and interest, debt service, and the draws and repayments on any revolving facility. It is distinct from the statutory accounts, which look backwards, and from the budget, which is a plan rather than a prediction.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The forecast runs on data pulled from the accounting system, the accounts receivable and payable ledgers, the bank feeds, and the payroll and tax calendars. Most teams assemble it in a spreadsheet, though larger treasuries use dedicated treasury management systems or a forecasting module inside their enterprise resource planning platform. Bank connectivity through formats such as MT940 and CAMT statements, or through open banking interfaces, determines how fresh the opening cash position is. The quality of the forecast depends far more on the reliability of those feeds than on the modelling technique layered on top.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The work starts with the opening bank position, then layers expected collections and disbursements by date. Receivables are usually grouped by customer and adjusted for how late that customer typically pays, using a payment behaviour history rather than the invoice due date. Payables are scheduled from purchase orders and contracts, with payroll, rent, tax and loan payments treated as near certain. Direct methods build the forecast line by line from these items, while indirect methods start from a profit figure and adjust for working capital movements. Machine learning now appears mainly in the collection side, where models predict the likely payment date for each open invoice and flag customers whose behaviour is drifting.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: The forecast is only as good as the assumptions written beside it, so version control, an audit trail and a named owner for each input matter as much as the arithmetic. Personal and financial data drawn from bank feeds and customer ledgers falls under data protection rules, and access should be limited to those who need it. Where a forecast is shown to lenders or a board, the assumptions behind it carry weight, and presenting a smoothed or optimistic view can become a disclosure problem. Segregation of duties between the person who runs the model and the person who approves payments is a standard control. Nothing here is legal, financial or investment advice, and any specific regulatory obligation should be checked with the appropriate professional.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The direction of travel is toward shorter cycles and more frequent refreshes, with daily rather than weekly positions becoming normal in larger groups. Bank data arriving through application programming interfaces is reducing the lag between a transaction and its appearance in the forecast. Prediction of customer payment timing is the area where machine learning has gained the most ground, and scenario and stress testing are being folded into the same tool rather than run separately. The persistent constraint is not the model but the discipline of keeping the underlying data clean and the assumptions honest.
